approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose evaluation budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation reflex added on top of it. In each session it keeps every molecule it has scored, breeds a fresh field of a hundred and sixty de novo offspring per announced batch of ten by fragment crossover and atom, bond and ring mutations of parents drawn from its high-scoring quantiles, and refuses anything that is not a single connected graph, is already known, or strays outside its inherited sulfur envelope. It then fits a Gaussian process to this session's accepted scores only, using count fingerprints with a generalized Tanimoto kernel, and draws one correlated posterior sample per batch position over the whole field; the ten molecules it sends to the oracle are the sequential maxima of those draws, each winner removed before the next position, so a molecule the model rates poorly on average can still win a position on a large sampled residual. The reflex earlier Children added is a stagnation counter: when three announced batches in a row fail to raise the session's own best score, the sampler is offered only the forty members of the field with the highest fitted posterior mean, and the whole field returns on the first batch that improves. Nothing bounds how long that narrowing can persist; in the Parent's worst session it governed the last seventeen batches of the run and that session never improved again.
approach.novelty: This node gives the narrowing a duration. The restriction keeps its trigger, its size, its ordering and its sampling law, but it may now govern at most five consecutive batches of one unbroken stall; from the sixth batch of that stall onward the sampler gets the full hundred-and-sixty-member field back for the rest of the episode, and the next improving batch re-arms the reflex exactly as before. Five is not a swept parameter: it is the longest unbroken stall that any session of the Parent survived while still gaining ground, and the Parent's own receipts show that the first five restricted batches of a stall carry essentially all of the restriction's realized gain while the batches beyond them consume a fifth of the stalled budget and return almost none of it. The siblings on this reflex have only ever pushed exposure the other way - holding the regime until two improving batches, both on the normal field and on the fourfold-widened one - and both lost; the other stall-time arms changed the sampler's randomness or how many candidates were bred for it to see. None of them put a bound on how long a stall may stay narrowed, which is the one axis of this reflex the Parent leaves completely open, and the bound deliberately keeps the part of the regime that measured positive instead of removing the reflex.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent is the lineage's new formal Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d, whose stall-time top-forty eligibility restriction is binary and unbounded in time: once this session's counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches reaches three, the eligible field stays cut to the forty highest posterior means of the unchanged 160-member fresh pool until some batch improves, however long that takes. Its complete fifteen-cell panel is +0.010577 over its mask-free code Parent n-1744a1494180 on all three seeds, but six cells fell, and its own analysis records exactly one structured regularity in those losses: every cell that held a restricted episode of eight or more announced batches lost (zaleplon_mpo seed 1 -0.035318 over 17 consecutive restricted batches, zaleplon_mpo seed 0 -0.035875 over 8, drd2_docking seed 2 -0.008280 over 9), while no gaining cell ever held an episode longer than five. Recomputing the exposure ledger read-only from the Anchor's own stall receipts and published trajectories reproduces its registered figures exactly (88 restricted of 435 announced batches, 29 episodes, 13 of 15 sessions, in-regime best-so-far increment sum 0.547037) and locates the waste by episode depth rather than by task: the first five restricted batches of an episode (69 batches) realize 0.526471 of increment, 0.007630 per batch, while the batches at depth six or more (19 batches, 190 oracle calls, 21.6 percent of the in-regime budget) realize 0.020566, 0.001082 per batch - 3.8 percent of the in-regime increment mass - and break the stall in 2 of 19 against 25 of 88 for the regime as a whole. The same depth split recomputed on the mask-free Parent n-1744a1494180, whose recomputation also reproduces its registered 91 restricted-equivalent batches and 0.476561 increment sum, costs only a factor of two (81 shallow batches at 0.005550 per batch against 10 deep batches at 0.002701), so depth conditioning alone does not explain a factor of seven: the masked deep tail is 2.5 times less productive per batch than the unmasked deep tail while being nearly twice as frequent. The extreme case is zaleplon_mpo seed 1, where the 12 batches past depth five spent 120 of that session's 290 optimizer evaluations without once beating the incumbent 0.438799. Both exposure experiments already run on this mechanism moved the opposite way and both lost (n-c7eb0cb7da3b held the regime until two consecutive improving batches, raising exposure from 88 to 162 restricted batches, -0.007929; n-f84de4030e74 did the same on the stall-widened pool, -0.004655), the sampling-law variants on this same trigger are refuted or neutral (n-189cd716f027 -0.009718, n-137ec411f54c -0.003338), and the one stalled-regime arm that gained changed the candidate set rather than the law (n-25b9a57765d8 +0.004664). How long the restriction may hold once it is on has never been varied.
hypothesis: Episode-bounded release of the stall-time eligibility restriction. A session-local counter of how many announced batches of the current stall episode have already been allocated with the restricted eligible set caps that restriction at five: a batch announced while the inherited consecutive non-improving counter stands at K=3 or more is restricted only while fewer than five restricted batches have been spent in this episode, and from the sixth such batch onward the inherited full 160-member availability mask is restored for every remaining batch of the episode. The inherited improving-batch reset clears both counters together, so the next episode re-arms the restriction from its own first batch and no new re-entry, escalation or hysteresis rule is introduced. The K=3 trigger, the M=40 (-posterior mean, pool index) top-mean ordering, the 160-member pool and target, the ten standard-normal rows and their shape, order and consumption count, the Cholesky jitter ladder, the residual scale, the per-pick mask update and the first-index tie rule are all exactly inherited, and a released batch runs the inherited unrestricted selection path unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Release ran exactly and tripled deep-stall yield, but only 1 of 3 forecast cells rose and the panel fell 0.00056: registered falsifier triggered
finding_summary.insights:
The campaign can now close the exposure axis of this reflex. Both directions have been measured on the same Anchor and the same panel: holding the restriction longer lost (-0.007929, and -0.004655 again on the widened pool), and releasing it sooner moves the panel -0.000562, inside law-free path noise. The depth ledger that motivated this arm is real and reproduces exactly - the first five restricted batches of an episode realize 0.007630 of incumbent gain per batch and the batches beyond them 0.001082, a factor of seven - but it is now shown not to be causal. Releasing the mask raised the deep-tail rate to 0.003427 per batch, which is the predicted direction, and the three cells that held the Anchor's long episodes still did not recover. The correlation between stall depth and loss was a property of those particular paths, not of the unreleased mask. No further rule on when the stall-time eligibility set opens or closes is worth an experiment on this Anchor.

The pick-level attribution says why, and it is the result that transfers. The region the release exists to restore did not pay for itself: not one of the 17 newly eligible picks ranked fortieth or worse ever beat the incumbent, the best of them reached 94 percent of it, and as a group they scored a median 25 percent of the incumbent against 95 percent for the released picks that the mask would have allowed anyway. Every one of the three stall-breaking improvements in a released batch came from a pick at posterior-mean rank 0, 2, 23 or 26 - inside the top forty. So the surrogate's ranking was not wrong about its own pool; the mask was discarding candidates that really were worse, and widening eligibility during a stall buys lottery tickets at the cost of oracle calls (17 of 90 released calls went to molecules worth a quarter of the incumbent). A stall on this method is not an allocation failure inside a good pool. It is a pool with nothing better in it: six of the nine released batches had the entire 160-member field available and still failed to improve.

The molecular review independently locates the pool's limit, and it is the proposal operator, not the allocator. Once a scaffold is found the generator cannot leave it - in 7 of the 15 sessions ten or fewer Murcko scaffolds cover the top quintile of proposals, in two cells only four, and one cell produced 51 distinct scaffolds in 290 proposals - because every move is a single-atom substitution. The three cells this node changed changed decoration, not chemotype: the winner it found in zaleplon_mpo seed 1 is the same N-fluorinated brominated indole-carboxamide core as the Anchor's with different substituents, and that score plateau is reached by three distinct molecules differing only in which halogen sits where. Under those conditions the realized spread of a single cell dwarfs any eligibility rule: a reference arm that changes no law at all and only perturbs the allocator's discarded draws reaches 0.482817 in zaleplon_mpo seed 1, +0.044 over the Anchor, where this deliberate release reached +0.013176, and the same 0.482817 is reached independently by four different nodes. The eight profile-matched recordings of zaleplon_mpo seed 0 span 0.414 to 0.459, twice the movement this arm produced there.

What that makes worth trying is a change of proposal mechanism, not another selection or eligibility rule on the same pool. The method needs a scaffold-level move - core replacement or ring-system hop - and fragment-level insertion of whole substituents from a small library, so that a stall has somewhere to go, together with a novelty or diversity term in the acquisition rather than the accepted-only posterior mean, which by construction prices similarity to what has already scored. Two cheaper waste channels are measured and independent of this arm: roughly 2 percent of the oracle budget goes to proposals of six or fewer heavy atoms that return no information, and the highest-scoring region of three objectives is built on nitrogen-halogen bonds the objective does not price out, so an admission-path valence rule would change what the same budget can buy. This node also leaves a usable protocol lesson: because the restriction is state-conditioned, a bound on it reproduces twelve of fifteen cells exactly, which makes the arm's whole result a three-cell contrast - a clean design, and also a demonstration that three cells of this benchmark cannot resolve an effect of the size this mechanism family produces.
finding_summary.results:
The duration cap executed exactly as registered, with nothing left to interpret at the implementation layer. Across all 435 announced batches of the fifteen cells the restriction governed 75 batches and lapsed for 9, and no stall episode anywhere in the panel contained a sixth restricted batch - against the Anchor's 19 restricted batches at depth six or more, including the session where the mask held the last 17 batches and 170 of 290 evaluations. In every restricted batch the eligible set was exactly the recomputed top forty of the posterior-mean ordering shrinking 40, 39, ... 31 across the ten picks; in every released batch it was the full field shrinking 160, ... 151 with nothing excluded; the logged episode counter matched an independent recount from the node's own accepted scores in all 435 batches, and the trigger, mask size, pool, draws and tie rules were untouched. Release fired in exactly the three cells forecast - zaleplon_mpo seeds 0 and 1 and drd2_docking seed 2 - each one first firing on precisely the batch the forecast named, and nothing diverged from the Anchor before that batch. The other twelve cells are identical to the Anchor record for record, all 300 records of each, so the whole panel movement sits in three cells.

The two behavioural predictions also came true. The released field genuinely re-opened: 17 of 90 released picks (18.9 percent) were molecules the mask had been excluding, ranked fortieth or worse by posterior mean, reaching rank 149, lifting the mean pick rank from 11.3 in the Anchor's matched deep tail to 25.0 and approaching the 28.7 percent share the allocator shows outside the stall regime at all. And the realized yield of those batches rose: 0.003427 of incumbent gain per released batch against the Anchor's 0.001082 in the same deep tail, a factor of 3.2 that also clears the mask-free depth-matched reference of 0.002701, with 3 of 9 released batches breaking their stall against 2 of 19. In the worst Anchor session the release broke a stall that had never broken: zaleplon_mpo seed 1 gained +0.013176 where the Anchor realized exactly zero over twelve deep batches and 120 evaluations.

The endpoint prediction failed. Of the three cells named in advance only zaleplon_mpo seed 1 rose; zaleplon_mpo seed 0 fell 0.021514 and drd2_docking seed 2 fell 0.000091, so one of three rose and the three sum to -0.008430 where the registration required at least two rising and a positive sum. The complete matched fifteen-cell panel came to 0.606468 against the Anchor's 0.607030, a change of -0.000562 where the arm needed +0.002 and had a ceiling of +0.005298. Both of those are registered falsifier branches and both triggered, so the route is refuted as registered, with no sweep of the release length and no change of the trigger or mask size authorized. The panel number itself is not evidence of harm: it lands inside the two-point law-free band for stall-gated arms on this lineage, [-0.003735, +0.009747].

The forensics of the losing cell are the informative part. In zaleplon_mpo seed 0 the released batches lost nothing at all - they realized exactly the Anchor's own +0.010205, at the same batch, to the same incumbent 0.401968. The 0.021514 disappeared one batch later, in the first unrestricted batch after the episode, where the Anchor's breeding stream found a jump that the already-diverged stream of this node did not. The cell did not pay for the release; it paid for having a different random path after it.

molecular.headline: Drug-sized fused aromatics that win by halogenating nitrogen: N-halogen in 87/87 and 64/87 of two top deciles, and no CF3 in 4350 proposals
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the generator emits one kind of molecule: a 24-32 heavy-atom, 3-5 ring, strongly aromatic compound (digest aromatic_atom_rate 0.964-0.977, ring_closure_rate 0.971-0.986) built by single-atom substitution around one scaffold it found early. The size, ring count and molecular weight (my RDKit reading of the 870 optimizer proposals per task: mean 24.3-31.6 heavy atoms, MW 365-461) all sit in ordinary medicinal-chemistry range, so the molecules look plausible at a glance. The functional groups do not. The decoration operator treats nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur as substitutable positions for F/Cl/Br exactly like carbon, and the scored surface pays for it: an N-halogen bond is in 410/870 proposals on one objective and 87/87 of its top decile, and 412/870 with 64/87 on another. Three structural capabilities are absent from all 4350 proposals: not one SMILES carries a stereo descriptor (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 on five tasks) though top-decile molecules average 0.75-1.98 unassigned tetrahedral centres; not one carries a formal charge (charged_rate 0.0 on five tasks); and not one contains a trifluoromethyl group, even where the top decile averages 3.4 fluorines per molecule placed one atom at a time. Compared with the Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d (paired_complete, three matched seeds), 12 of the 15 trajectory files are byte-identical, so this is the Parent's chemistry; the three cells that differ (zaleplon_mpo seeds 0 and 1, drd2_docking seed 2) differ by stream position rather than by new chemotype. In zaleplon_mpo seed 1 the Child inserts one extra low-scoring candidate, O=C(Nc1ccncc1)c1ccncc1 at 0.00002, after which the same molecules reappear shifted one position, and the cell's best becomes the N-hydroxy anilide Cc1cc2c(c(C)c1CN)c(Br)c(C(=O)N(O)c1ccccc1)n2F at 0.45198 instead of the Parent's N-(pyridin-2-yl) amide at 0.43880.

per_task.generated_character: The flattest and most converged set: mean 24.3 heavy atoms, MW 368, 3.0 rings of which 2.7 aromatic and only 0.28 aliphatic (0.02 in the top decile). Essentially a single scaffold family, an indole-2-carboxanilide (Murcko scaffold O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1 covers 40 of the 58 molecules in seed 0's top quintile, and seed 1's top quintile has only 4 distinct scaffolds), decorated with methyl, ethyl and methoxy on the benzo ring, a halogen at the pyrrole 3-position, and a halogen or hydroxyl on the amide nitrogen. No sp3 ring anywhere in the high scorers, no basic centre, no stereochemistry and no charge.
liabilities: N-chloro, N-bromo and N-fluoro anilides such as C(=O)N(Br)c1ccccc1 are electrophilic halogenating reagents, not candidate compounds
N-halogenated pyrrole nitrogen (n2F, n2Br) on every top-decile molecule; an N-halo azole is an N-halogenating agent
the single best molecule carries an N-hydroxy anilide (C(=O)N(O)c1ccccc1), a hydroxamic-type N-O bond, stacked on top of an N-F pyrrole
the final batch regresses to N-hydroxy pyrrole (n2O) and a cyclopropane-fused indole, Cc1cc2c3c(C)c1Cc3c(C(=O)C(=O)N(Cl)c1ccccc1)n2O at 0.34174
alpha-keto anilides (C(=O)C(=O)N) in the seed-2 cluster add a reactive glyoxamide to an already reactive N-Cl amide
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere (1 of 870 proposals), so the aryl-cyano group that the top scaffold's aryl ring could carry is never tested
no N,N-dialkylamide side chain: 0 of 870 proposals contain an acetamide with two N-alkyl groups
no fused azine with a ring N-N bond: aromatic N-N in 4 of 870 proposals and 0 of 87 in the top decile, so pyrazolo-fused bicyclics are unreachable
no basic amine on a ring: basic ring nitrogen in 0 of 87 top-decile molecules, and no ionizable centre at all
no saturated ring appended to the aromatic core (top-decile aliphatic rings 0.02 per molecule)
no defined stereochemistry: the entire 870-molecule set is written without a single stereo descriptor
per_task.score_gradient_reading: 0.0 to 0.4520 with median 0.3265. The bottom is bare fragments (F, NCl, C=CCl all exactly 0.0). Score climbs with aromatic ring count (bottom-decile mean 1.71 to top-decile 2.99), heavy atoms (17.1 to 24.8) and logP (3.03 to 4.80), but the sharpest separator is heteroatom halogenation: an N-halogen bond appears in 410 of 870 proposals and in 87 of 87 top-decile molecules, chiefly as an N-halo pyrrole nitrogen (n2F, n2Br, n2Cl) or an N-halo anilide. The top of the run is a plateau of halogen permutations on one molecule: three distinct SMILES share the identical score 0.4519753.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the five (mean 31.6 heavy atoms, MW 461, 4.18 rings of which 3.48 aromatic, TPSA 123) and three mutually unrelated per-seed clusters. Seed 0 converges on a fused thioxo-pyrimidinone cage linked to a quinazoline that carries an aryl hypofluorite, O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 at 0.85615. Seed 1 converges on a benzoxazinone diaryl ether carrying two aryl nitriles, a dichloropyridine and an S-Br bond. Seed 2 converges on a bis(C-nitroso) anilide fused to a four-membered-ring cage. Seed 0's top quintile holds 10 distinct Murcko scaffolds, seed 1's holds 7.
liabilities: aryl hypofluorite O-F bonds (the cc(OF)c motif) in the three highest-scoring molecules; an aryl O-F bond is not a stable compound
an alpha-chloro ether, C(F)OCCl, on the same top scorers: a fluoro-chloromethyl ether is a direct alkylating agent
C-nitroso groups, two per molecule, in 56 percent of the top decile (C(N=O)Nc2cc3c(N=O)cc2-3)
a transannular bond drawn inside a benzene ring (cc3c(N=O)cc2-3) gives a Dewar-benzene type bicyclo[2.2.0] cage; 24 percent of the top decile contains an all-aromatic four-membered ring
thiocarbonyl c(=S) thioureas and a formate/thioformate ester (CCOC=O, CCOC=S) in the final batch
the seed-1 cluster carries an S-Br sulfenyl bromide and an OC#N cyanate ester, both hydrolytically unstable
missing_features: no sulfonamide or sulfone anywhere (0 of 870 proposals) and only 8 of 870 carry a plain secondary N-H amide linker
no carboxylic acid or acidic isostere: 0 acids and 0 tetrazoles in 870 proposals
no basic amine centre: basic ring nitrogen in 1.1 percent of the top decile against 12.6 percent of the bottom, so the search strips basicity out
no defined stereochemistry although top-decile molecules average 0.75 unassigned tetrahedral centres
no trifluoromethyl or geminal-difluoro blocking group beyond 9 of 870 incidental CF2 cases
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The floor is 0.5, not 0: single atoms and diatomics (Cl, C=C, CBr, C#CF) all score exactly 0.50, so the entire optimized band is 0.50 to 0.8561 with median 0.5965. Above the floor the score tracks size and polarity (heavy atoms 19.9 to 32.0 bottom to top decile, TPSA 69 to 132, rotatable bonds 2.9 to 8.5, logP 1.9 to 4.8) and a biaryl-linked azine core. Two reactive classes rise with score rather than falling: C-nitroso presence goes from 6.9 percent of the bottom decile to 56.3 percent of the top, and molecules containing a ring of four atoms or fewer go from 6.9 to 57.5 percent.

per_task.generated_character: The most drug-like-looking series of the five and the one with the clearest pharmacophore. The top decile is a lipophilic basic amine: 2.0 aromatic plus 1.2 aliphatic rings, 27.4 heavy atoms, MW 461, logP 5.43, TPSA 31.5, with a basic sp3 amine in 87 of 87 molecules and a basic ring nitrogen in 83 of 87. The recurring motif is a 2-aryl-2-alkyl hexahydropyrimidine tethered by an ethylene to a poly-substituted benzene, best at 0.99999 with CCCc1c(Br)cc(Br)cc1CCN1CCCNC1(CC)c1cccc(Cl)c1. Seed 2 converges instead on a chromane bearing an N-vinyl azetine enamine (7 scaffolds in its top quintile).
liabilities: the N-C-N aminal of the hexahydropyrimidine (253 of 870 proposals, 78 of 87 in the top decile) hydrolyzes back to a ketone and a diamine
logP 5.43 and MW 461 in the top decile with two or three aryl halogens: outside the usual lead-like range
alpha-halo alcohols C(O)F and C(O)Cl on top scorers, which are latent acyl halide or carbonyl equivalents
an N-chloromethyl amine (N(CCl)) and an S-Cl group (C(N)(SCl)) in the final batch, both direct alkylating or sulfenylating agents
the seed-2 series builds a strained N-vinyl azetine enamine (C1=CCN1) as the basic centre
missing_features: no aromatic heterocycle in the top decile beyond benzene and pyridine: 0 imidazoles, 0 tetrazoles and no fused heteroaromatic bicyclic among the high scorers
no stable saturated diamine such as a piperazine or piperidine: the basic ring is reached only through an N-C-N aminal carbon (78 of 87 top-decile molecules)
no amide or sulfonamide retained alongside the basic amine, so a basic-amine-plus-amide chemotype is never sampled
no trifluoromethyl or other metabolically blocking group in 870 proposals; lipophilicity is tuned only with Br, Cl and alkyl
no stereochemistry written on the 1.54 unassigned tetrahedral centres per top-decile molecule, so the docking-relevant configuration is undefined
no formal charge anywhere, so the protonated form the pharmacophore implies is never represented
per_task.score_gradient_reading: 0.00017 to 0.99999, the widest span of the five. The starting pool is 3,5-dichlorobenzenesulfonyl prolinamides at 0.0002 to 0.0016. The gradient is almost entirely the removal of polar amide chemistry and the installation of a lipophilic basic amine: sulfonamide presence falls from 50.6 percent of the bottom decile to 0 of 87 in the top, carboxylic acid 35.6 to 0 percent, amide 43.7 to 0 percent, TPSA 88.0 to 31.5, oxygen count 4.9 to 0.5, while basic sp3 amine rises from 17.2 to 100 percent and aryl halide from 70 to 100 percent. The score rewards a cation-plus-lipophile pair, and the optimizer buys the last few thousandths with extra bromine and propyl groups on the aryl ring.

per_task.generated_character: The one halogen-free set: digest halogen_rate 0.1011 against 0.81 to 0.98 on the other four, and 0.11 halogen atoms per molecule. The converged motif is a 2-propylquinolin-4-yl amine fused onto a bridged glycine-anhydride cage, best at 0.24240 with CCCc1cc(N2C3CC4=C(NCN4C(=O)CN(C)C3=O)C2CC)c2ccccc2n1. Top-decile molecules average 1.84 bridgeheads and a largest ring of 8.1 atoms: 93 percent contain a ring of eight atoms or more and 55 percent a ring of four or fewer. Score rises with ring count (3.64 to 4.97), aliphatic rings (1.36 to 2.86), bridgehead atoms (0.56 to 1.84), amide presence (33 to 93 percent) and basic ring nitrogen (24 to 85 percent), while halogens are actively disfavoured (aryl halide 9.2 percent of the bottom decile, 0 of 87 in the top). per_task.score_gradient_reading: 7.7e-27 to 0.76586 with median 0.1815, so the median molecule sits far below the best and the distribution is strongly skewed. The bottom is bare fluorine chemistry (F, FF, CF at 0.0). Score tracks fluorine count (bottom decile 0.92 to top decile 3.36) more than anything else, and the way the optimizer buys fluorine is by bonding it to nitrogen: heteroatom-halogen bonds rise from 19.5 percent of the bottom decile to 73.6 percent of the top, and N-halogenated aromatic nitrogen from 17.2 to 71.3 percent. Secondary contributors are a basic N-H pyrrolidine (18.4 to 51.7 percent) and heavy-atom count (19.4 to 27.0).

transferable_gaps.evidence: An N-halogen bond appears in 410 of 870 and 412 of 870 proposals on two objectives, and in 87 of 87 and 64 of 87 of their top-decile molecules; N-halogenated aromatic nitrogen alone covers 71.3 percent of one top decile. Aryl O-F bonds appear in the three single highest-scoring molecules of a third objective, and an S-Br bond in a fourth cluster. These are halogenating reagents rather than candidate compounds, so the highest-scoring region of three objectives is chemically unreal.
transferable_gaps.gap: The decoration operator attaches halogens to nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur as freely as to carbon, and the search converges on those bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Restrict the substitution operator so a halogen may only be bonded to carbon, or apply a cheap valence-and-alert filter to proposals before they consume an oracle call. The same budget then buys carbon-framework edits, which is where the remaining score on these surfaces has to come from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4350 optimizer proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group and not one contains three adjacent aromatic fluorines, even on the objective whose top decile averages 3.36 fluorines per molecule and whose score rises monotonically with fluorine count. The same set contains no tetrazole (0 of 4350) and essentially no pyrazole (1 of 4350).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no multi-atom substituent insertion: it can only add or swap one atom at a time, so common grouped substituents are unreachable.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add fragment-level proposal moves that attach a whole substituent or a whole ring from a small library (CF3, sulfonamide, acid isostere, N-N azole) in one edit, alongside the existing atom-level moves, so a reward for a grouped feature is reachable in one step instead of three improbable ones.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of the 4350 proposed SMILES carry an @ or @@ descriptor, which the digest confirms as stereocentre_rate 0.0 on every one of the five objectives, while the top-decile molecules carry 0.75 to 1.98 unassigned tetrahedral centres each. Every three-dimensional-sensitive score the run obtained was obtained from a configurationally undefined molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemistry is never part of the search space: the generator writes no stereo descriptors at all.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Either emit and mutate stereo descriptors as part of the representation, so configuration is a dimension the optimizer can move in, or canonicalize each proposal to one defined isomer before scoring so the reported score belongs to a specific compound.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of the 4350 proposals carry a formal charge, which the digest confirms as charged_rate 0.0 on all five objectives. Carboxylic acids and sulfonamides survive only in the low-scoring starting-pool region of one objective (51 acids and 76 sulfonyl groups across 870 proposals, 0 of each in its top decile), and no objective's high scorers carry any acidic group at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits a charged or ionizable species, and the search actively strips acidic groups out.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add operators that install acidic groups and ionizable centres, and represent the protonation state the pharmacophore implies, so zwitterionic and salt-forming chemotypes are reachable instead of being pruned the moment the surface prefers lipophilicity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 57.5 percent of one objective's top decile and 46.6 percent of another objective's whole proposal set contain a ring of four atoms or fewer, and 24.1 percent of that top decile contains an all-aromatic four-membered ring: the cc3c(N=O)cc2-3 motif is a transannular bond across a benzene ring, a Dewar-benzene type bicyclo[2.2.0] cage. RDKit sanitizes these, so nothing in the pipeline objects.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits can draw a bond between two atoms of an existing aromatic ring, producing strained cages rather than fused systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Have the ring-closure operator refuse bonds whose two endpoints already lie in the same aromatic ring, and enforce a minimum new-ring size, so ring-forming edits produce fused, bridged or spiro systems that a chemist could draw a route to.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An N-C-N aminal carries the basic centre in 78 of 87 top-decile molecules on one objective and in 25 of 87 on another, and 182 to 253 of 870 proposals per objective contain one; N-O single bonds reach 9.2 percent of a top decile and a cyclic enamine 86.2 percent of another. The molecules therefore present the right pharmacophoric atoms on connectivity that would not survive in solution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds its best pharmacophores out of hydrolytically labile heteroatom-carbon-heteroatom linkages instead of stable equivalents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the operator set stable alternatives for the same pharmacophore (a saturated diamine ring with carbon between the nitrogens separated by two bonds, an amine in place of an aminal) and penalize or filter N-X-N and N-O linkages at proposal time, so a found pharmacophore is expressed on makeable connectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 101 of the 4350 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms, including bare atoms (F, Br, Cl, C), diatomics (FF, FCl, NCl, OO, CBr) and C#C. Each of these scores at or very near its objective's floor, and on one objective the floor is a constant 0.5 that every fragment receives identically, so the evaluation carries no information about any edit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Roughly two percent of the oracle budget goes to degenerate single-atom and diatomic proposals that return no gradient information.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bound the deletion and fragmentation operators by a minimum heavy-atom count, or reject below-threshold products before the oracle call, so the deleted-to-nothing branch of the edit distribution stops consuming a fixed budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In 7 of the 15 sessions the top quintile of proposals is covered by 10 or fewer Murcko scaffolds, and in two cells by only 4. One objective's score plateau is three distinct molecules at the identical score 0.4519753 differing only in which halogen sits where, and one cell produced only 51 distinct scaffolds across all 290 of its proposals. Across seeds, by contrast, the converged scaffolds are completely unrelated, so the early scaffold choice, not the objective, decides the endpoint.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a scaffold is found the generator cannot leave it: the proposal distribution has no scaffold-level move.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add a scaffold-level proposal move (core replacement or ring-system hop) and a diversity term over the proposal distribution, so single-atom substitution is not the only route out of a local scaffold and an unlucky early commitment is recoverable.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
